A naive calculation evaluating specific vertices or edges (proxies) fails silently when the mesh changes. Homology solves this algebraically by taking the quotient of 'cycles' (closed loops) by 'boundaries' (loops that are the edge of a surface). This quotient explicitly drops all dependence on the specific grid arrangement, yielding Betti numbers that are perfectly invariant under any structural reordering.
